description: THE STRAWBERRY HALL 8/10\\n\\nArguably a pub that is one of the most talked about in Dublin while remaining a well-kept secret of sorts, the Strawberry Hall deserves the plaudits it receives. Despite being as isolated as a Dublin pub really can be, tucked away alongside the Liffey and under the huge Westlink toll bridge, this place has relied on its authenticity and high standards of customer service to bring in the trade, and you can see that it‚Äôs working. The pub is one of the capital‚Äôs oldest dating back to the 1800‚Äôs, and just outside the M50, has a feeling of being the only watering hole for miles around. The fact that they run a shuttle service to Lucan and Castleknock only adds to the rural feel while ensuring plenty of regulars remain at the bar.\\n\\nUpon first look the pub doesn‚Äôt exactly take your breath away with its architectural beauty; however the inside is a different story. The front bar has more character and characters in it than some of the busiest bars in the city. All four heads turned to look at me upon entering ‚Äì a sign that the pint might be of a high standard. Instantly engaged, it wasn‚Äôt long till I felt at home, by which time walking behind the bar counter to get into the huge beer garden felt normal. The huge beer garden and its numerous benches mean this is a place where many a summer evening should be spent.\\n\\nThe pint was as enjoyable as the rest of the pub, so good even the novelty strawberries on the walls started to look tasty. Plenty of cream, volume and taste on point until the last drop, you can see why the locals might not be shouting about this gem of a pub - keeping it all for themselves.\\n\\n#guinness #guinnessstorehouse #guinnessadvisor #lovingdublin #dublincity #dublinviews #pints #beers #lucan #strawberrybeds

description: This picture depicts a German Sd.Kfz. 164 Panzerjager Nashorn of Schwere Panzerjager Abteilung 655  on the Eastern Front,1943. 1943 was the major turning point for the Germans and axis in Europe during WW2, with Axis held Africa having fallen, The Italian succession in September, and the failure of the Germans to win in the battle of Kursk. The Germans thus started a major fighting retreat on the Eastern Front, never to mount another major assault, reinforced the Italian front with German troops so as to block the allied advance, and started to reinforce the Atlantic Wall defenses in preparation of any allied attempt at landing there. (Which we all know would happen in June of 1944.) I will give the Germans credit though, as their retreat in the East was very well done, and inflicted very many Soviet casualties. The Soviets had so many men though, that this barely hurt them. This Nashorn has tick (tally) marks on its main gun, signifying how many enemy tanks it took down, which seems to be quite a few. This just again shows the consequence the Germans had of opening two fronts in the war. If the USSR was never invaded, the majority of German troops, which fought there, could have been used in the West in Italy and later France. Maybe the Soviets would have even fought along side the Germans like in 1939. Who knows how things might have turned out, but it sure would have played out differently. #War #history #vintage #retro #rustic #usa #america #england #france #germany #italy #russia #japan #boat #tank #batlle #worldwar2 #worldwarii #ww2 #wwii #worldwar2foryou Also go follow @the_ww2_memoirs @world.war.europe @ww2_history9 @world_war_2_militaria @_world_war_2_pictures @militaryhistory @ww2_german_history and @ww2dailyhistory

description: BATU BERSURAT TERENGGANU - Prasasti Kedatangan Islam .\\n.\\nPada tahun 1887, Batu Bersurat telah dijumpai di kawasan Padang Tara di tepi Sungai Tara di Kampung Buloh, Kuala Berang, Hulu Terengganu. Kemudian pada tahun 1902, batu ini di jumpai pula oleh Saiyed Husin bin Ghulam Al-Bukhari seorang ahli perniagaan di bahagian tangga surau Kampong Buloh yang dijadikan alas membasuh kaki untuk naik ke tangga surau tersebut. Batu ini telah patah sebahagian di sebelah atasnya.\\n.\\n.\\nSaiyed Husin meminta Penghulu Ali dan orang kampung mengangkat dan meletakkannya di atas rakit untuk dibawa ke Kuala Terengganu. Sampai di sana batu ini dipersembahkan ke Kebawah Duli Yang Maha Mulia Sultan Zainal Abidin iii dan kemudian batu itu diletakkan di atas Bukit Puteri. Padg tahun 1922, Timbalan Penasihat Inggeris di Terengganu Encik H.S Peterson meminta seorang jurufoto berbangsa Jepun N. Suzuki mengambil gambar dan di hantar kepada C.O. Blegden untuk dibuat pembacaan.\\n.\\n.\\nBatu ini ditulis di dalam bahasa Melayu dengan tulisan jawi bertarikh 702 Hijrah. Tulisan pada batu ini menerangkan Islam sebagai agama rasmi dan hukum-hukum Islam mengenai perbuatan maksiat dan kenyataan2 palsu berserta hukuman mengikut taraf seseorang. Pada tahun 1923, batu ini telah dihantar ke Muzium Singapura dengan jalan pinjaman. Apabila Muzium Negara di Kuala Lumpur siap dibina, batu tersebut telah di bawa ke Kuala Lumpur sebagai pinjaman dari Muzium Raffles Singapura.\\n.\\n.\\nPada 12 Februari 1987, kerajaan Terengganu menulis surat kepada jabatan muzium negara menyatakan hasrat untuk mendapat kembali batu bersurat tersebut untuk di jadikan bahan pameran di Muzium Negeri Terengganu. Pada tahun 1991, jumaah Menteri telah memutuskan memgembalikan Batu Bersurat kepada Kerajaan Negeri Terengganu\\n(Sumber : Muzium Negeri Terengganu)\\nPicture by @misimencarimelayu\\n.\\n#misimencarimelayu \\n#warisanmelayu \\n#malayheritage
